classification: P0 correctness defect in approximate KV reuse under device pressure

workload.note: the source context and the target context are identical, so an exact copy must reproduce the dense output bit for bit

conclusion.trigger: a competing approximate registration combined with tight device capacity, i.e. real device memory pressure at the moment the reuse request runs
not_the_trigger: residency tier of the reused object (device and host both corrupt under pressure and both are correct without it)
device to host demotion (diag6 corrupts with no demotion at all)
tight capacity by itself (diag7 is correct at the same 3400 tokens without the competing registration)
prefill path numerical nondeterminism (see control-exact-cache-guardrail.json, 16/16 exact matches)
mechanical_evidence_that_still_passes: store record, device byte, host byte and lease gauges
zero orphans and a clean post-round reset
conclusion.failing_evidence: recovered output diverges from the matched dense arm although the source and target contexts are identical
conclusion.suspected_area: the device slots that back a pinned approximate reuse source are not protected from the allocation and eviction performed for the same request in allocate_recovery_slots; this needs a dedicated fix and dual review, and was deliberately not patched speculatively

impact.p6_h: the generic host roundtrip canary cannot be marked valid; Phase 6 Exit is blocked on data fidelity, not on accounting
impact.cl1: CL1 ran every arm at rho_logical_demand=2.0, so all approximate arms executed under pressure; the CL1 quality_8_token_match and first_token_match failures are confounded with this defect and cannot be attributed to cross-context approximation error
impact.cl1_verdict: practical family = NONE remains the procedurally correct result of the frozen promotion rule, but its causal attribution is invalid until this defect is fixed and CL1 is re-run
impact.phase7: Phase 7 must not start on this substrate; the recovery correctness contract is unproven under pressure
